$comment: THIRD-PARTY PLATFORM SPECS, each with the date it was last verified.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. 49% of this site's search impressions are year-qualified
queries ('vercel free tier bandwidth 100gb 2025', '...limit 100gb 2026'). In the
Vercel cluster it is 69%. Half the demand is explicitly asking AS OF WHEN, and
the page answering it dated 17 of its 319 sentences. A spec sentence that does
not carry its own date cannot be lifted into an answer as a dateable fact.
WHY IT IS DATA AND NOT PROSE. Writing 'as of August 2026' inline fifty times is
prose-carried fact-state: the same class that produced the PageSpeed drift and
the fabricated 95 on /services/ecommerce. Typed once, rendered everywhere, one
edit moves every date on the page.
THESE ARE OTHER COMPANIES' NUMBERS. We do not control them and they change
without notice. Every value here must be read off the vendor's own published
page and carry the URL it came from. Never carry a value forward on memory.
ENFORCEMENT. scripts/spec_freshness.py warns at 90 days and FAILS the build at
180. A stale third-party price presented as current is the same defect class as
a withdrawn metric that keeps rendering.

vercel-hobby-fast-data-transfer.label: Fast Data Transfer
vercel-hobby-fast-data-transfer.qualifier: published as a fair-use guideline, not an itemised plan allowance

vercel-hobby-fast-origin-transfer.label: Fast Origin Transfer
vercel-hobby-fast-origin-transfer.qualifier: the cap most comparisons omit; reached before the 100 GB figure on an uncached or image-heavy site

vercel-pro-price.label: Pro plan price
vercel-pro-price.qualifier: platform fee including one deploying seat and a usage credit; added seats and usage are extra

googlebot-crawl-size-limit.label: Googlebot crawl size limit
googlebot-crawl-size-limit.value: the first 2MB of a supported file type
googlebot-crawl-size-limit.qualifier: reduced from 15MB; past the cutoff Googlebot stops the fetch and only the downloaded part is considered for indexing. Each referenced resource is fetched separately under the same cap. PDFs: 64MB

webflow-basic-price.label: Basic site plan price
webflow-basic-price.qualifier: billed yearly, per site, plus tax; custom domain, 300 static pages, 10 GB bandwidth. The monthly-billing toggle did not re-render when this was read, so no monthly figure is verified

webflow-premium-price.label: Premium site plan price
webflow-premium-price.qualifier: billed yearly, per site, plus tax; the tier that adds the CMS, site search and code components. Previously named the CMS plan

webflow-team-price.label: Team platform plan price
webflow-team-price.qualifier: annual contract required. This is a platform plan, charged on top of the per-site plans, not instead of them. Google's AI Overview stated this as $2,500 a year when checked

webflow-optimize-addon.label: Optimize add-on price
webflow-optimize-addon.qualifier: priced by page views, and charged separately from the site plan

webflow-localize-essential.label: Localize Essential price
webflow-localize-essential.qualifier: covers 1 to 3 locales in total, not $9 per locale. Localize Advanced is $29 a month for 1 to 10

webflow-analyze-addon.label: Analyze add-on price
webflow-analyze-addon.qualifier: priced by sessions, and charged separately from the site plan

shopify-storefront-api-protocol.label: Storefront API protocol
shopify-storefront-api-protocol.qualifier: Shopify states there is no REST API for storefronts

shopify-storefront-api-content.label: Content available through the Storefront API
shopify-storefront-api-content.value: pages, blogs and articles, alongside products, collections, cart, checkout, search and customer accounts
shopify-storefront-api-content.qualifier: this is why Shopify can serve a headless site as well as a headless shop

woocommerce-store-api-scope.label: Store API scope
woocommerce-store-api-scope.value: unauthenticated cart, checkout and product endpoints at /wp-json/wc/store/v1/
woocommerce-store-api-scope.qualifier: WooCommerce describes it as public endpoints for customer-facing cart, checkout and product functionality

woocommerce-rest-api-scope.label: REST API scope
woocommerce-rest-api-scope.value: authenticated admin resources only, with no cart or checkout endpoints
woocommerce-rest-api-scope.qualifier: products, orders, customers, coupons, refunds, tax rates and reports; a headless storefront needs the separate Store API

wix-headless-price.label: Wix Headless entry price
wix-headless-price.qualifier: Wix states a premium plan is required to unlock payments, in-depth analytics and custom domains

wix-headless-solutions.label: Business solutions available headlessly
wix-headless-solutions.value: eCommerce, bookings, events, memberships, CMS and blog
wix-headless-solutions.qualifier: Wix states these sit under a single auth model and a consistent API pattern

squarespace-api-scope.label: Developer API scope
squarespace-api-scope.value: nine back-office Commerce APIs, with no content, page or storefront API
squarespace-api-scope.qualifier: Analytics, Contacts, Discounts, Inventory, Orders, Products, Profiles, Transactions and Webhook Subscriptions

webflow-cloud-frameworks.label: Frameworks deployable to Webflow Cloud
webflow-cloud-frameworks.qualifier: deployed to Webflow infrastructure either standalone or mounted on an existing Webflow site at a path

webflow-devlink-direction.label: What DevLink moves
webflow-devlink-direction.value: Webflow components exported as React components into an external codebase
webflow-devlink-direction.qualifier: Webflow describes DevLink as the interface between external codebases and Webflow

gohighlevel-api-scope.label: Public API modules
gohighlevel-api-scope.value: CRM and contacts, conversations, calendar and events, opportunities, payments and webhooks
gohighlevel-api-scope.qualifier: Blogs and Funnels APIs are listed in the developer portal; whether they return renderable page content was not established
